title: Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking from Wormholes in Holography
authors: Taishi Kawamoto, Kenya Tasuki, Masahito Yamazaki
abstract: We study strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SWSSB) at finite temperature and its implications in holography. SWSSB is a novel critical phenomenon that arises only in mixed states. We demonstrate SWSSB with the BTZ black hole and show that, in the bulk, it is realized through wormhole geometries connecting the two copies in the thermofield-double construction. We point out that SWSSB can be recast as an emergence of global symmetries under ensemble averaging. We further examine the interplay between SWSSB and the swampland program, and propose a new swampland conjecture for quantum-gravity theories involving ensemble averages.
summary: This paper explores Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SWSSB) using holographic models dual to black hole physics. By calculating specific correlation functions like the Rényi-2 correlator, the authors demonstrate that SWSSB occurs when comparing different thermal ensembles. This leads to a novel Swampland conjecture connecting symmetry breaking to fundamental constraints in quantum gravity theories.
main_problem: The study investigates Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SWSSB) at finite temperature within the framework of holography.
main_result: Non-zero Rényi-2 and Wightman correlators in the large distance limit demonstrate SWSSB, which is linked to the emergence of weak symmetries via ensemble averaging. The authors propose a new Swampland conjecture regarding this phenomenon in quantum gravity.
method: The analysis employs holographic methods using the AdS/CFT correspondence, calculating correlation functions (Rényi-2 and Wightman) by implementing projection operators through twisted boundary conditions on bulk fields.
model_or_system: The model involves a 2D CFT dual to an Einstein-Chern-Simons theory coupled with probe matter in the bulk geometry of a BTZ black hole, analyzed at finite temperature.
key_observables: Rényi-2 correlator ($R^{(2)}$) and Wightman correlator ($C_W$), which are used to diagnose the presence or absence of symmetry breaking.
important_parameters: Finite temperature ($ eta=1/T$), large distance limit ($|x-y|	o\infty$), and the chemical potential $\mu$ associated with charge conservation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on large-$N$ factorization, specific limiting procedures for correlation functions, and the assumption that SWSSB is diagnosed by these correlators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-contractible cycle wrapping the BTZ horizon and show how different field types (neutral vs. charged) interact with boundaries in the bulk geometry.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining SWSSB and setting up the holographic model, calculating correlation functions using twisted boundary conditions, demonstrating the non-zero nature of $R^{(2)}$ and $C_W$, and concluding by formulating a Swampland conjecture based on these findings.
why_interesting: While deeply rooted in quantum gravity/holography, the core concept—symmetry breaking diagnosed via correlation functions in mixed states—is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and open quantum systems dynamics.
